Pool one effect size per study into a random-effects estimate per feature

stats_meta.Rd

Pool one effect size per study into a random-effects estimate per feature (DerSimonian-Laird), with heterogeneity, direction agreement and the largest leave-one-out change.

Each feature is pooled on its own by mzLib's RandomEffectsMeta.Pool, with the DerSimonian-Laird (1986) moment estimator of the between-study variance, as metafor's rma(method = "DL") does (mzLib matches metafor to 1e-8 relative). Every row also says how many studies agree in direction and how far the estimate moves when any one is dropped - the two checks a reader of a pooled result asks for first.

Usage

stats_meta(studies, confidence = 0.95, timeout = 60)

Arguments

studies

A data.frame with one row per study and columns feature, estimate and standard_error. A feature's studies need not be adjacent. The standard error must be positive.

confidence

Coverage of the reported interval, as a fraction (0 to 1).

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Value

An mzlibr_meta_analysis: records, a data.frame with one row per feature in order of first appearance - feature; studies pooled; estimate, standard_error, confidence_low and confidence_high (units of the study estimates); p_value (a fraction, 0 to 1, normal reference, not adjusted across features); tau2 (squared units of the study estimates); q (a chi-square statistic) and i_squared (a fraction, 0 to 1), both NA for one study; direction_agree and direction_disagree (studies); and leave_one_out_max_delta (units of the study estimates, NA for one study). Also study_count studies, feature_count features, confidence (a fraction, 0 to 1), row_count rows and caveats.

With few studies

DerSimonian-Laird with a normal reference: the interval and p-value do not widen for few studies (no Hartung-Knapp adjustment), so treat a pooled estimate from two or three studies with care. Send records$p_value to stats_adjust to adjust across features.

Wraps

Wire verb stats meta. Generated from the bridge's verb spec stats.meta.yaml (bridge commit c0cc92372aad) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

  • RandomEffectsMeta.Pool in mzLib/StatisticalModels/RandomEffectsMeta.cs at mzLib 0a808fec

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

studies (wire --stdin)

string[]; required; range >= 1 line. One study per line, tab-separated: feature, estimate, standard_error. No header. A feature's lines need not be adjacent; features are reported in order of first appearance. The estimate must be finite and the standard error finite and positive. Blank lines are skipped.

confidence

float; in fraction (0 to 1); default 0.95; range (0, 1). Coverage of the reported interval, as a fraction.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

study_count

int; in studies; never NA. Study lines read, over every feature.

feature_count

int; in features; never NA. Distinct features; the table's row count.

confidence

float; in fraction (0 to 1); never NA. The coverage used, as a fraction.

row_count

int; in rows; never NA. Equal to feature_count.

column_names

string[]; never NA. The table's columns.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. One row per feature.

caveats

string[]; never NA. Three static caveats.

Columns of records

feature

string; never NA. As given on stdin.

studies

int; in studies; never NA. Studies pooled for this feature.

estimate

float; in units of the study estimates; never NA. Random-effects pooled estimate.

standard_error

float; in units of the study estimates; never NA. Standard error of the pooled estimate.

confidence_low

float; in units of the study estimates; never NA. Lower bound of the interval: estimate - z standard_error.

confidence_high

float; in units of the study estimates; never NA. Upper bound of the interval.

p_value

float; in fraction (0 to 1); never NA. Two-sided p-value of the pooled estimate against 0, normal reference. Not adjusted across features.

tau2

float; in squared units of the study estimates; never NA. Between-study variance (DerSimonian-Laird); 0 for one study, and exactly 0 whenever q <= studies - 1.

q

float; in chi-square statistic (studies - 1 degrees of freedom); NA when one study: no heterogeneity to measure. Cochran's Q.

i_squared

float; in fraction (0 to 1); NA when one study. Share of the variation attributed to heterogeneity, as a fraction in [0, 1].

direction_agree

int; in studies; never NA. Studies whose estimate has the pooled estimate's sign (a 0 estimate counts for neither).

direction_disagree

int; in studies; never NA. Studies with the opposite sign.

leave_one_out_max_delta

float; in units of the study estimates; NA when one study. Largest absolute change in the pooled estimate from dropping any one study.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

stdin empty; a line without exactly 3 tab-separated fields; an empty feature name; an estimate that is not a finite number; a standard error that is not finite and positive (mzLib's refusal, reclassified, naming the feature); --confidence not strictly between 0 and 1, or given without a value

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

never expected

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • DerSimonian-Laird with a normal reference: the interval and p-value do not widen for few studies (no Hartung-Knapp adjustment), so treat a pooled estimate from two or three studies with care.

  • A feature with one study is reported with tau2 = 0 and q, i_squared and leave_one_out_max_delta null.

  • Each feature is pooled on its own and p_value is not adjusted across features; send the p_value column to stats adjust.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.stats.meta

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::stats::meta_with with MetaOptions

  • R (mzLibR): stats_meta

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.3.0; mzLibRust not yet shipped; mzLibR not yet shipped.

Not yet verified

The spec records these as open. They are listed rather than hidden:

  • Rust and R spellings are proposals until those bindings ship the verb.

  • The example's studies are mzLib's metafor reference cases (Test/StatisticalModels/ReferenceData/dl_inputs.tsv), copied verbatim to pkg/python/tests/fixtures/stats/metafor_dl_inputs.tsv. They are constructed cases, not proteomics data.

References

  • doi:10.1016/0197-2456(86)90046-2: the moment estimator of the between-study variance (DerSimonian and Laird, Control Clin Trials 7:177, 1986)

  • doi:10.18637/jss.v036.i03: metafor, whose rma(method = 'DL') mzLib reproduces to 1e-8 relative (Viechtbauer, J Stat Softw 36(3), 2010)

See also

stats_fit, stats_adjust

Examples


# metafor's own DerSimonian-Laird reference cases, from mzLib's test data:
inputs <- read.delim(system.file("extdata", "stats", "metafor_dl_inputs.tsv", package = "mzLibR"))
studies <- data.frame(feature = inputs$case, estimate = inputs$yi, standard_error = inputs$sei)
pooled <- stats_meta(studies)
pooled$records[, c("feature", "studies", "estimate", "tau2", "direction_agree")]
#>         feature studies   estimate       tau2 direction_agree
#> 1   homogeneous       5  0.3096950 0.00000000               5
#> 2 heterogeneous       6  0.2512721 0.07516970               5
#> 3   two_studies       2 -0.2000000 0.06000000               1
#> 4  random_eight       8  0.1069573 0.09113603               6
